title: Use of class, field, or method that is not compatible with JDK 8.
summary: It is an experimental check, so Error Prone does not turn it on by default.

title: Duration.getNano() only accesses the underlying nanosecond adjustment from the whole second.
summary: Error Prone turns it on by default.

title: Prefer duration.toSeconds() over duration.getSeconds().
summary: Error Prone turns it on by default.

title: Use of java.time.Duration.withNanos(int) is not allowed.
summary: Error Prone turns it on by default.

title: Use of java.time.Duration.withSeconds(long) is not allowed.
summary: Error Prone turns it on by default.

title: Instant.getNano() only accesses the underlying nanosecond adjustment from the whole second.
summary: Error Prone turns it on by default.

title: LocalDateTime.getNano() only access the nanos-of-second field. It's rare to only use getNano() without a nearby getSecond() call.
summary: Error Prone turns it on by default.

title: LocalTime.getNano() only accesses the nanos-of-second field. It's rare to only use getNano() without a nearby getSecond() call.
summary: Error Prone turns it on by default.

title: Period.getDays() only accesses the "days" portion of the Period, and doesn't represent the total span of time of the period. Consider using org.threeten.extra.Days to extract the difference between two civil dates if you want the whole time.
summary: Error Prone turns it on by default.

title: Java.time APIs that silently use the default system time-zone are not allowed.
summary: Error Prone turns it on by default.

title: Date has a bad API that leads to bugs; prefer java.time.Instant or LocalDate.
summary: Error Prone turns it on by default.

title: Abstract and default methods are not injectable with javax.inject.Inject.
summary: Error Prone turns it on by default.

title: @javax.inject.Inject cannot be put on a final field.
summary: Error Prone turns it on by default.
